Its services are mainly used by oil companies, especially for [[ONGC]]. The company listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]].{{cite web |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2005/04/26/stories/2005042602060200.htm |title=Aban Loyd to buy 3 more jack-up rigs – Gets shareholders' nod to raise $100 m |work=Business Line}}{{cite web |url= http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/iw/2006/03/19/stories/2006031900470900.htm|title= Aban Loyd Chiles Offshore: Buy |work=The Hindu Business line}}{{cite web | last1= Narasimhan| first1= T. |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/aban-offshore-reports-consolidated-net-loss-of-rs-193-85-crore-in-the-september-2020-quarter-120111101345_1.html |work=Business Standard India |date=11 November 2020}}{{Cite web|last1=Com |first1=Moneycontrol |title=Aban Offshore Balance Sheet, Aban Offshore Financial Statement & Accounts|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/financials/abanoffshore/balance-sheetVI/AO04|access-date=2021-12-18|website=moneycontrol.com|language=en}} ==Controversies== ===Central Bank of India Insolvency Case=== [[Central Bank of India]] filed an application under [[Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016|Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016]], against Aban Offshore Ltd, for defaulting on loans. The bank aimed to initiate insolvency proceedings for recovery of outstanding dues.{{cite web | last=Raj | first=Shubham | title=Aban Offshore spikes as Central Bank withdraws insolvency petition | website=Moneycontrol | date=12 September 2022 | url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/stocks/aban-offshore-spikes-as-central-bank-withdraws-insolvency-petition-9164941.html | access-date=27 August 2025}}{{cite web | last= | first= | title=Central Bank withdraws insolvency application against Aban Offshore | website=Business Standard | date=1 October 2019 | url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/central-bank-withdraws-insolvency-application-against-aban-offshore-119100101297_1.html | access-date=27 August 2025}} In August 2022, Aban Offshore entered into a one time settlement agreement with Central Bank of India. Under the agreement, Aban Offshore paid the outstanding principal of {{INRConvert|121.78|c|year=2022}} to the bank.{{cite web | last= | first= | title=Central Bank withdraws IBC case as Aban Offshore pays one-time settlement | website=Business Standard | date=12 September 2022 | url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/central-bank-withdraws-ibc-case-as-aban-offshore-pays-one-time-settlement-122091201107_1.html | access-date=27 August 2025}} After the payment and settlement, the Central Bank of India withdrew its insolvency case against Aban Offshore Ltd at the [[National Company Law Tribunal]]. ===Aban Loyd Chiles Customs Case=== In 2015, the [[Directorate of Revenue Intelligence]] seized the vessel{{clarify|reason=what vessel?|date=September 2025}} on grounds of alleged unauthorized deployment beyond the contractual zone. The company challenged the imposition of penalties and customs duty, arguing that the use and deployment of Aban-ICE complied with amended essentiality certificates from governmental authorities such as the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons.{{cite web | title=SUPREME COURT OF INDIA |website=sci.gov.in| url=https://api.sci.gov.in/jonew/judis/29804.pdf | access-date=27 August 2025}} ===Sanctions and OFAC Settlement=== Aban Offshore's Singapore subsidiary was penalized by the [[Office of Foreign Assets Control|U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control]] for violating Iranian sanctions regulations in 2017. The violation involved re-exporting U.S.-origin goods to Iran without proper authorization. Aban agreed to a settlement and paid a civil monetary penalty.{{cite web | title=Settlement Agreement between OFAC and Aban Offshore Limited; Settlement Agreement between OFAC and an Individual and the Alliance for Responsible Cuba Policy Foundation | website=Office of Foreign Assets Control | date=27 June 2008 | url=https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20170112_44 | access-date=27 August 2025}}{{cite web | last1= Narasimhan| first1= T. E.| title=Aban Offshore's receivables from Iran dip $36 mn after lifting of sanctions | website=Business Standard | date=5 June 2017 | url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/aban-offshore-s-receivables-from-iran-dip-36-mn-after-lifting-of-sanctions-117060500172_1.html | access-date=27 August 2025}} == References == {{reflist}} == External links == * {{Official website|http://www.abanoffshore.com/}} [[Category:Service companies of India]] [[Category:Drilling rig operators]] [[Category:Companies based in Chennai]] [[Category:1986 establishments in Tamil Nadu]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1986]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Multinational companies headquartered in India]]

Aban Offshore (formerly Aban Loyd Chiles Offshore Ltd.) is an Indian multinational offshore drilling services provider headquartered in Chennai. Its services are mainly used by oil companies, especially for ONGC. The company listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
The group has also ventured into construction, offshore and onshore drilling, wind energy and power generation, Information Technology enabled services, hotels and resorts, tea plantations and in marketing.
